title: RARE: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Modeling

problem.claim: Domain-specific intelligence requires specialized knowledge and sophisticated reasoning, while LLMs struggle with knowledge hallucination and inadequate reasoning capabilities.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need for efficient discovery and modeling of reasoning patterns in data.

contributions.claim: RARE is a paradigm that extracts and models reasoning patterns from data as salient and learnable tokens.
RARE stores domain knowledge in retrievable repositories while encoding reasoning patterns within LLMs.
RARE injects retrieved knowledge into training prompts with masked losses to make implicit reasoning patterns salient and shift learning toward contextualized reasoning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe RARE as a novel paradigm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that lightweight RARE-trained Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B models achieved state-of-the-art performance in extensive experiments.
The authors report that these lightweight models rivaled retrieval-augmented Gemini-3-Pro-Preview and GPT-5.1 models with trillion-scale parameters.

narrative_sequence.summary: Domain-specific intelligence is difficult because LLMs face hallucination and reasoning limitations.
RARE is proposed to discover and model reasoning patterns as salient, learnable tokens.
The approach separates retrievable domain knowledge from internally modeled reasoning patterns and uses masked-loss training prompts.
RARE aims to reduce reliance on parameter-intensive memorization and emphasize higher-order reasoning patterns.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance from lightweight RARE-trained models and a broader shift toward external knowledge bases paired with compact reasoning models.

source_observation.claim: The approach combines retrievable external domain knowledge with internalized reasoning patterns in the model.

interpretation.claim: Separating knowledge storage from reasoning-pattern modeling may reduce the need to encode all domain knowledge in model parameters.

application.claim: For domain-specific systems, consider pairing maintainable external knowledge bases with compact models optimized for reasoning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which domains, retrieval conditions, or failure cases determine when this design is effective.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, tasks, baselines, or evaluation metrics used in the experiments.
The abstract does not report quantitative performance values or statistical analyses.
The abstract does not describe the retrieval sources, tokenization procedure, masking scheme, or training details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification, reproducibility, or generalization beyond the reported experiments.
